author: assistant
text:
Opened the new [brainstorming Activity](C:/Users/hmhri/Desktop/repos/HAI/.hai_env/activities/00000000_000000_active/README.md). Your choice is recorded: roles describe responsibilities and limits, supported by skills; additional contents remain open.

My initial recommendation is:

**A skill describes how to perform a task. A role describes the responsibility under which that task is performed.**

A role can add several useful things beyond a collection of skills:

- **Professional perspective:** what the executor should pay attention to. An architect considers system boundaries and tradeoffs; a business analyst considers business needs and unanswered questions.
- **Expected outcomes:** what the role must deliver and what makes its work satisfactory.
- **Decision boundaries:** which choices the executor may make within the user's authorization and which require a handoff or human decision.
- **Working relationships:** what information the role needs from others and what it must return to them.

For example, both an analyst and an architect could use the same create-design-package skill. The skill supplies the method and document structure. Their roles establish different responsibilities for the contents.

The folders themselves cannot establish the distinction. The [Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/specification) allows instructions, scripts, references, assets and additional directories.

I would use this provisional ownership rule:

| Material | Default home |
| --- | --- |
| Reusable task procedures, scripts and templates | Skill |
| Responsibilities, professional perspective and handoff obligations | Role |
| Conventions used throughout the project | Shared project/framework location |
| Task-specific formats and rules | Skill, or a shared contract when several capabilities use them |
| Settings | The capability or service that owns them, stored once |

**A role can still have its own conventions, procedures or scripts when they serve a responsibility specific to that role.** I would avoid requiring those folders, duplicating skill methods there, or forcing every small procedure into a separate skill.

That gives us a useful direction: lighter roles assembled from reusable capabilities, with room for meaningful role-specific instructions. The exact composition and ownership rules still need discussion; no HAI implementation has changed.

author: assistant
text:
Workflows describe the **company process**. Roles describe **job responsibilities**. Skills provide **methods for doing the work**. An AI agent executes the assignment, and an Activity holds the actual work and its records.

I suggest this division. The workflow rules already exist; the role/skill division remains our design proposal.

| What needs defining | Where it belongs | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Responsibility, professional perspective and limits | Role | The analyst must identify unresolved business decisions. |
| Available capabilities | Role references skills | The analyst can clarify requirements and write acceptance scenarios. |
| Reusable task instructions and internal procedures | Skill | How to conduct clarification and document the findings. |
| Scripts and templates supporting that method | Skill | A requirements template and its checking script. |
| Role-specific conduct across several skills | Role | The architect must explain material tradeoffs. |
| Process steps, their order and responsible roles | Workflow | Clarification precedes architecture and implementation. |
| Assignment for this particular step | Workflow | Clarify this customer request using the supplied material. |
| Required inputs, outputs, filenames and locations for each handoff | Workflow | Produce requirements.md where the architecture step expects it. |
| Named results, selection conditions and next steps | Workflow | Clarified goes to architecture; questions-needed returns for clarification. |
| Business retry/loop limits | Workflow | Allow at most three clarification attempts. |
| Conventions applying across capabilities or processes | Shared project/framework conventions | Common naming and document structures. |
| Settings | Their actual owner, stored once | Several Git skills use one Git integration configuration. |
| Actual outputs, execution status and history | Activity/workflow run | The files and accepted results from one execution. |

A workflow step still needs a clear instruction. It states **what to accomplish in this process**, while a skill supplies the reusable detailed method. The workflow should reference that method rather than reproduce it.

For your customer-request example:

| Workflow step | Role | Skill used |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Clarify the request | Business analyst | Clarify requirements |
| Design the solution | Solution architect | Create a design package |
| Implement the approved design | Software developer | Implement a change |
| Update documentation | Specification manager | Maintain specifications |

These skill names are illustrative. Whether a workflow explicitly requires a particular skill or lets the role choose one is still an open design decision.

Physical placement would be:

- **Roles:** `.hai_env/roles/<name>/ROLE.md`.
- **Skills:** currently `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`; the final HAI installation location remains undecided.
- **Workflow definitions:** `.hai_env/workflows/<name>.md`, one file per workflow.
- **Run records and handoff files:** `<activity>/workflow-runs/<run-id>/`, with separate step attempts.
- **Shared HAI conventions and runtime tools:** `.hai/conventions/` and `.hai/tools/`.

Durable product changes and documentation keep their normal project locations. Run evidence stays with the run. Every workflow run remains inside one Activity, and only one run executes at a time.

Roles can retain genuinely role-specific resources, but neither roles nor workflows need to duplicate skill implementations. The comparison is saved in the [discussion document](C:/Users/hmhri/Desktop/repos/HAI/.hai_env/activities/00000000_000000_active/results/role-skill-discussion.md).

author: assistant
text:
Agreed. I recommend **one folder per run, plus a step name and execution number in each intermediate filename**:

```text
run-123/
  clarify-001-requirements.md
  design-001-solution-design.md
  clarify-002-requirements.md
  design-002-solution-design.md
```

Count each execution of a step, rather than a whole loop: branches may repeat only some steps.

- **Advantages:** no overwriting, clear history, and files remain identifiable when copied elsewhere.
- **Costs:** longer names, and downstream steps must receive the exact accepted file path. They should never guess which file is latest.

Separate attempt folders with stable filenames are another option, but filenames lose that context when copied out of their folders. Your proposed filename distinction is useful.

The workflow could declare a naming pattern such as `clarify-{attempt}-requirements.md`; HAI would assign the number and resolve the downstream input. Final published outputs could retain stable names, with publication handled separately from intermediate attempts.

That last distinction is my proposal, not an agreed rule. Your other four answers are saved, and formal clarification is paused.
